purpose: Find a mathematically simpler or more robust formulation for the paper, preserving its intended measurement questions. Produce defensible recommendation, not empirical validation or a novelty claim.
boundary: Finite task/person/type-of-work sets; measurable fractional allocations a>=0 with sum over tasks and work types <=1 per person almost everywhere; bounded calendar time. Observations are exact interval sums or justified finite lower/upper person-hour limits. Sampling is a distinct observation process, not exact data.
targets: Attainable labour totals in specified target windows; retained-output/person-hour productivity; design-unbiased estimation and precision with fixed predictions and known sampling probabilities.
units: calendar time hours; cell labour person-hours; retained output specified reference-score units; probabilities dimensionless.
criteria: Compare current LP with published theorem/alternative and simpler baseline
Specify what each improvement buys and fails to buy
Separate proof from finite checks and empirical applicability
Keep original approach if rivals do not improve required quantities

tractability.scope: research prototype, not production service guarantee
tractability.encoding: rational inputs, test bit length <=16, real-valued formal theorem
tractability.numerical_policy: exact rational verification for published examples and certificates; floating solver diagnostics separate from proofs
tractability.accuracy: zero gap when an exact certificate is claimed; otherwise record unresolved gap

proof_authority: Published theorems with independently reviewed hypotheses and paper proofs; exact finite computations. MAS arbitrary new-theorem Lean acceptance unavailable (no isolated comparator/pinned toolchain); do not issue formal acceptance or substitute registry shear benchmarks.
coordinator_disclosure: Coordinator knows the complete baseline and has nominated generic LP duality/robustness and linear-fractional programming literature for its own search. No candidate is prescribed to workers. All workers receive same baseline; initial work independently; later proposals delivered through Rust bus.
